objects.description: Type alias for basic_memory_buffer<char> commonly used to collect formatted output without dynamic allocations for small sizes.
A lightweight output helper that writes formatted data either to a FILE* or to a fmt internal buffer<char>. It does not own the underlying target.
A convenience wrapper holding a std::string and exposing a buffer-compatible writer. Allows implicit conversion to fmt::writer to format directly into the internal string.
Exception type thrown for formatting errors. Inherits std::runtime_error and forwards constructors.
A portable 128-bit unsigned integer fallback implemented using two uint64_t halves. Provides arithmetic and bitwise operations used internally when native 128-bit types are unavailable.
An internal stand-in type for 128-bit floating point. It is a real type alias to __float128 when available, otherwise an empty struct used for overload selection.
Converts a UTF-8 string_view to UTF-16 (host endian) and stores the result in an internal basic_memory_buffer<wchar_t> with trailing NUL. Provides accessors and conversion operators.

An internal arbitrary-precision non-negative integer used by Schubfach/Dragon algorithms for formatting floats. Stores base-2^32 digits with an exponent, supports multiplication, shifting, comparison, pow10 building and division by subtract loops.

Internal binary floating-point decomposition containing an unsigned significand f and exponent e representing f * 2^e. Provides constructors from IEEE754 floats and indicates predecessor-closer state for correct rounding.
Helper structure computing the final output size and zero padding amount for integer formatting given digits, prefix, and specs. Used to avoid template bloat.
A small utility to format an integer into an internal buffer with minimal overhead and expose the result as data()/c_str()/str(). Useful for fast integer-to-string conversions.
A type-erased holder for a formatting argument used in localized formatting paths. Wraps a basic_format_arg<context> and exposes a visit method. Special-cases float128 to avoid heavy dependencies.
Public wrapper type to request byte-sequence formatting through its corresponding formatter<bytes> specialization.
Internal representation of a decimal floating number as a pointer to digit buffer, its length, and base-10 exponent for later writing with grouping and padding.
Visitor that extracts an unsigned width/precision from a format argument or reports an error if not an integer, used for dynamic specs resolution.
Sentinel/empty type used where a value is intentionally absent (e.g., variant-like or placeholder in APIs). Trivially constructible and comparable only via user code if needed.
A lightweight non-owning view over a contiguous character sequence. Mirrors a subset of std::basic_string_view; used pervasively for format strings and string-like inputs.
A minimal output iterator that appends code units to an internal fmt buffer. Used as the default sink for formatting routines.
Primary formatting context for char output. Holds the output iterator, the type-erased argument pack, and an optional locale reference.
Parsing context passed to formatter<T>::parse to walk the format string segment for a single replacement field. Tracks next automatic index and allows switching to manual indexing.
Holds parsed formatting flags common to many types (align, sign, alt form, localized, uppercase, dynamic width/precision and fill). Stores compact bitfields plus a small fill buffer.
Extends basic_specs with concrete width and precision values (possibly dynamic at parse-time). Used for built-in and string formatting.
Type-erased holder for a std::locale object to avoid including <locale>. Convertible to bool indicating presence; get<Locale>() retrieves the stored locale (definition elsewhere).
Traits for iterator_buffer doing no counting and no limiting; provides default behavior.
Iterator buffer trait that enforces a fixed output limit while tracking the total attempted write count. Used by format_to_n.
Read-only view over a collection of formatting arguments. Uses a compact descriptor to store types inline for small arg-count cases; supports name lookup.
Helper return type for formatting into fixed-size char arrays; converts to char* while detecting truncation.

functions.name: fmt::to_string
functions.signature:
template <size_t SIZE>
FMT_NODISCARD auto fmt::to_string(const basic_memory_buffer<char, SIZE>& buf) -> std::string
functions.description: Converts a fmt::basic_memory_buffer<char, SIZE> to an std::string by copying its current contents.
requirements: buf must reference a valid basic_memory_buffer<char, SIZE> whose data() and size() reflect the current buffer contents.
The resulting string length is buf.size(); no null terminator from the buffer is required.

functions.name: fmt::to_string
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename = enable_if_t<std::is_integral<T>::value>>
FMT_NODISCARD FMT_CONSTEXPR_STRING auto fmt::to_string(T value) -> std::string
functions.description: Converts an integral value to std::string using fmt’s fast integer formatting.
requirements: T must be an integral type (including bool).
No formatting options are applied; decimal formatting is used.
Function is constexpr-friendly when supported (FMT_CONSTEXPR_STRING).

functions.name: fmt::system_error
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
auto fmt::system_error(int error_code, format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args) -> std::system_error
functions.description: Builds and returns a std::system_error whose message is produced by fmt::format(fmt, args...) and whose error_code is error_code in the generic_category.
requirements: error_code should be a valid system error code (e.g., errno).
fmt must be a valid fmt::format_string matching args’ types (compile-time checked).
Does not perform I/O; it only constructs and returns the exception object.

functions.name: fmt::vformat
functions.signature: inline auto fmt::vformat(locale_ref loc, string_view fmt, format_args args) -> std::string
functions.description: Formats according to fmt and args using the specified locale loc, returning the result as std::string.
requirements: fmt must be a valid format string for the supplied args.
args must remain valid for the duration of the call.
loc controls localized formatting for locale-sensitive specifiers.

functions.name: fmt::format
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
FMT_INLINE auto fmt::format(locale_ref loc, format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args) -> std::string
functions.description: Formats arguments with the given locale and returns the resulting std::string. The format string is compile-time checked.
requirements: fmt must be a valid fmt::format_string for the provided args types.
Produces localized output for locale-aware parts using loc.

functions.name: fmt::vformat_to
functions.signature:

auto fmt::vformat_to(OutputIt out, locale_ref loc, string_view fmt, format_args args) -> OutputIt
functions.description: Formats into an output iterator using the specified locale and returns the advanced iterator.
requirements: OutputIt must model an output iterator for char (i.e., writable).
out must refer to a valid output destination with enough capacity/validity for all produced characters.
fmt must be valid for args; args must stay valid during the call.
The returned iterator points past the last written character.

functions.name: fmt::format_to
functions.signature:
template <typename OutputIt, typename... T,

FMT_INLINE auto fmt::format_to(OutputIt out, locale_ref loc, format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args) -> OutputIt
functions.description: Formats arguments with a locale directly into the provided output iterator and returns the advanced iterator. The format string is compile-time checked.
requirements: OutputIt must be an output iterator over char and remain valid for all writes.
fmt must be a valid fmt::format_string matching args types.
loc applies to locale-aware formatting.

functions.name: fmt::formatted_size

FMT_NODISCARD FMT_INLINE auto fmt::formatted_size(locale_ref loc, format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args) -> size_t
functions.description: Computes the number of characters that would be produced by formatting with the given locale and arguments, without producing output.
requirements: fmt must be a valid fmt::format_string for the provided args types.
Returns the count of code units (chars) that formatting would generate.

functions.name: fmt::format_system_error
functions.signature: FMT_API void fmt::format_system_error(detail::buffer<char>& out, int error_code, const char* message) noexcept
functions.description: Formats a system error message of the form "<message>: <system-message>" for the given error_code and appends it to out.
requirements: out must reference a valid mutable buffer<char>.
message should point to a valid null-terminated C-string (non-null) to be included as the prefix.
Function is noexcept; callers must not rely on exceptions for error reporting.

functions.name: fmt::report_system_error
functions.signature: FMT_API void fmt::report_system_error(int error_code, const char* message) noexcept
functions.description: Reports a system error (typically without throwing), intended for use in contexts like destructors where exceptions must not be thrown.
requirements: message should be a valid null-terminated C-string (non-null) describing the context.
Function is noexcept; no exceptions will be thrown.

functions.name: fmt::vsystem_error
functions.signature: FMT_API auto fmt::vsystem_error(int error_code, string_view fmt, format_args args) -> std::system_error
functions.description: Constructs and returns a std::system_error with message formatted from fmt and args and error_code from the OS (generic_category).
requirements: fmt must be a valid format string for the provided args.
args must remain valid during the call.
Suitable when the argument pack is already type-erased (v-API).

functions.name: fmt::format_int::size

functions.name: fmt::format_int::data

functions.name: fmt::format_int::c_str
functions.signature: FMT_CONSTEXPR20 auto fmt::format_int::c_str() const -> const char*
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the character buffer containing the formatted number with a terminating null character appended.

functions.name: fmt::format_int::str
functions.signature: inline auto fmt::format_int::str() const -> std::string

functions.name: fmt::basic_memory_buffer::get_allocator
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t SIZE, typename Allocator>
auto fmt::basic_memory_buffer<T, SIZE, Allocator>::get_allocator() const -> Allocator
functions.description: Returns a copy of the allocator associated with this basic_memory_buffer instance.
requirements: The buffer object must be valid. No other preconditions.

functions.name: fmt::basic_memory_buffer::resize
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t SIZE, typename Allocator>
FMT_CONSTEXPR void fmt::basic_memory_buffer<T, SIZE, Allocator>::resize(size_t count)
functions.description: Resizes the buffer to contain count elements. For POD types, new elements may be left uninitialized.
requirements: count must not exceed the maximum representable size; internally uses try_resize which may reallocate.
After resizing up, element initialization is not guaranteed for POD types.

functions.name: fmt::basic_memory_buffer::reserve
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t SIZE, typename Allocator>
void fmt::basic_memory_buffer<T, SIZE, Allocator>::reserve(size_t new_capacity)
functions.description: Ensures the buffer’s capacity is at least new_capacity; may reallocate using the associated allocator.
requirements: new_capacity must be representable and not exceed allocator’s max_size.
Iterators/pointers into the old storage may be invalidated if reallocation occurs.

functions.name: fmt::assert_fail
functions.signature: FMT_NORETURN FMT_API void fmt::assert_fail(const char* file, int line, const char* message);
functions.description: Aborts the program on an internal assertion failure, reporting the source file, line and a message. Intended for use by the fmt library macros to signal logic errors in debug builds.
requirements: file must be a valid, null-terminated C-string identifying the source file (may be used for diagnostics).
line must be the source line number associated with the failure.
message must be a valid, null-terminated C-string describing the failure.
This function never returns (noreturn).

functions.name: fmt::report_error
functions.signature: FMT_NORETURN FMT_API void fmt::report_error(const char* message);
functions.description: Reports a format-related error either at compile time (via static analysis paths) or at runtime by throwing a format_error (or otherwise aborting depending on build). It is used internally by parsing/validation code to signal invalid format strings or argument issues.
requirements: message must be a valid, null-terminated C-string describing the error.
This function never returns (noreturn).

functions.name: fmt::basic_string_view::data
functions.signature: template <typename Char> constexpr auto fmt::basic_string_view<Char>::data() const noexcept -> const Char*

requirements: The returned pointer may be null if the view is default-constructed (size()==0 and data()==nullptr).
The pointer is not null-terminated unless the referenced sequence is; do not read past size().
The view does not own the data; the underlying data must outlive the view usage.

functions.name: fmt::basic_string_view::size
functions.signature: template <typename Char> constexpr auto fmt::basic_string_view<Char>::size() const noexcept -> size_t

functions.description: Returns an iterator (pointer) one past the last element of the view.
requirements: If size()==0, begin()==end().
Do not dereference the returned iterator; it refers past the last element.

functions.description: Safely converts a floating-point value from type From to type To. Preserves NaN and infinities. For finite inputs, checks whether value fits in To's range; if out of range, sets ec=1 and returns To{}.
requirements: From and To must be floating-point types (enforced via static_assert).
Caller must pass an int ec by reference and check it after the call; ec==0 indicates success.

template <typename Duration>
inline auto gmtime(sys_time<Duration> time_point) -> std::tm
functions.description: Convenience overload that converts a std::chrono::time_point based on system_clock to a UTC std::tm by first converting to time_t with overflow-checked casts, then calling fmt::gmtime(std::time_t).
requirements: Argument must be a sys_time<Duration> (time_point over system_clock).
May throw format_error if conversion of time_point to std::time_t overflows or is otherwise not representable (via detail::duration_cast and the underlying gmtime overload).
Callers should be prepared to handle exceptions (format_error).

functions.name: fmt::detail::range_begin
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
auto fmt::detail::range_begin(const T (&arr)[N]) -> const T*
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the first element of a C array. Intended as a generic begin() helper for array ranges used by the formatting library.
requirements: arr must be a reference to a C array of known bound N.
The returned pointer becomes invalid if the array goes out of scope.

functions.name: fmt::detail::range_end
functions.signature:
template <typename T, size_t N>
auto fmt::detail::range_end(const T (&arr)[N]) -> const T*
functions.description: Returns a pointer one past the last element of a C array. Intended as a generic end() helper for array ranges used by the formatting library.
requirements: arr must be a reference to a C array of known bound N.
The returned pointer becomes invalid if the array goes out of scope.
Do not dereference the returned pointer; it points past the end.

functions.name: fmt::detail::for_each
functions.signature:
template <typename Tuple, typename F, size_t... Is>
FMT_CONSTEXPR void fmt::detail::for_each(fmt::detail::index_sequence<Is...>, Tuple&& t, F&& f)
functions.description: Invokes f(get<Is>(t)) for each index Is in the provided index_sequence. Low-level helper to iterate tuple-like elements by index.
requirements: Tuple must support std::get<Is>(t) for each index in the sequence.
F must be callable as f(element) for each corresponding element type.
Side effects of f will occur in left-to-right order of indices as expanded.

functions.name: fmt::detail::for_each2
functions.signature:
template <typename Tuple1, typename Tuple2, typename F, size_t... Is>
void fmt::detail::for_each2(fmt::detail::index_sequence<Is...>, Tuple1&& t1, Tuple2&& t2, F&& f)
functions.description: Invokes f(get<Is>(t1), get<Is>(t2)) for each index Is in the provided index_sequence, iterating two tuple-like objects in lockstep.
requirements: Tuple1 and Tuple2 must both support std::get<Is>(...) for each index in the sequence and have at least that many elements.
Corresponding element types must be acceptable to F: f(elem1, elem2) must be valid for each index.
t1 and t2 must remain valid for the duration of calls to f.

functions.name: fmt::join
functions.signature:
template <typename It, typename Sentinel>
auto fmt::join(It begin, Sentinel end, fmt::string_view sep) -> fmt::join_view<It, Sentinel>
functions.description: Creates a lightweight view that formats the iterator range [begin, end) with elements separated by sep when passed to fmt formatting functions.
requirements: [begin, end) must denote a valid range; incrementing from begin to end must be well-defined.
The value type referenced by It must be formattable with fmt (a suitable formatter must exist).
sep is a string_view; its referenced character data must remain valid until formatting is performed.
Iterators/Sentinel must be copyable/movable as required by join_view and the formatter.

functions.name: fmt::join
functions.signature:
template <typename Range, FMT_ENABLE_IF(!fmt::is_tuple_like<Range>::value)>
auto fmt::join(Range&& r, fmt::string_view sep)
    -> fmt::join_view<decltype(fmt::detail::range_begin(r)), decltype(fmt::detail::range_end(r))>
functions.description: Creates a view that formats all elements of an iterable range r separated by sep. This overload deduces begin/end via fmt::detail::range_begin/range_end.
requirements: Range must not be tuple-like (SFINAE constraint).
Range must be iterable via either member begin()/end(), ADL begin/end, or C array and produce iterators/sentinels forming a valid range.
Element type of r must be formattable with fmt.
r must outlive the formatting operation that consumes the returned view.
sep's referenced character data must remain valid until formatting is performed.

functions.name: fmt::join
functions.signature:
template <typename Tuple, FMT_ENABLE_IF(fmt::is_tuple_like<Tuple>::value)>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto fmt::join(const Tuple& tuple FMT_LIFETIMEBOUND, fmt::string_view sep)
    -> fmt::tuple_join_view<Tuple, char>
functions.description: Creates a view that formats a tuple-like object with its elements separated by sep when used with fmt formatting. Uses per-element formatters.
requirements: Tuple must be tuple-like (std::tuple_size and std::get are valid).
Each element type of Tuple must be formattable with fmt.
The passed tuple object must outlive the use of the returned view (lifetimebound).
sep's referenced character data must remain valid until formatting is performed.

functions.name: fmt::join
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
auto fmt::join(std::initializer_list<T> list, fmt::string_view sep)
    -> fmt::join_view<const T*, const T*>
functions.description: Creates a view that formats all elements of an initializer_list separated by sep when used with fmt formatting.
requirements: T must be formattable with fmt.
The initializer_list and its elements must remain alive until formatting consumes the returned view (do not pass a temporary initializer_list to a longer-lived context).
sep's referenced character data must remain valid until formatting is performed.

functions.name: fmt::make_printf_args
functions.description: Builds a format_arg_store holding references to the supplied arguments for use with the printf-style formatting context (basic_printf_context<Char>). Intended to be passed to fmt::vsprintf/fmt::vfprintf and similar v-variants. Stores references to the original arguments; no formatting occurs here.
requirements: Char must be either char or wchar_t (per basic_printf_context static assertion).
Arguments are stored by reference; each referenced object must outlive any subsequent formatting call that consumes the returned store.
Callers must pass lvalues (including const lvalues); rvalues are not accepted because the parameters are T&... (non-const lvalue references to possibly-const types).
Use the returned object only with the matching printf-style context (basic_printf_context<Char>).

functions.name: fmt::vsprintf
functions.signature:
template <typename Char>
inline auto fmt::vsprintf(basic_string_view<Char> fmt,
                          typename vprintf_args<Char>::type args)
    -> std::basic_string<Char>;
functions.description: Formats according to the printf-style format string fmt using a pre-built argument pack (vprintf_args<Char>) and returns the formatted result as std::basic_string<Char>. This is the v-variant that accepts a precompiled argument list.
requirements: Char must be either char or wchar_t (per basic_printf_context).
fmt must point to a valid, null-terminated-like character sequence view; the format string must use printf-style specifiers supported by this implementation.
args must have been created for the same Char using fmt::make_printf_args (or an equivalent fmt::make_format_args with basic_printf_context<Char>).
The number and types of arguments in args must be compatible with the format specifiers in fmt; otherwise formatting reports errors (e.g., via report_error).

functions.name: fmt::sprintf
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
inline auto fmt::sprintf(string_view fmt, const T&... args) -> std::string;
functions.description: Formats according to the printf-style format string fmt and returns the result as a std::string (narrow, char). This is a convenience wrapper that builds the argument pack and calls fmt::vsprintf.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string recognized by this implementation.
The number and types of args must match the format specifiers in fmt.
Arguments are passed by const reference; if you pass references to objects, they must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: fmt::vfprintf
functions.description: Formats according to the printf-style format string fmt using a pre-built argument pack and writes the output to the FILE stream f using std::fwrite. Returns the number of characters written on success, or -1 if writing fewer than the produced characters occurs.
requirements: f must be a valid, non-null pointer to an open FILE suitable for writing.
Char must be either char or wchar_t (per basic_printf_context).
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string recognized by this implementation.
args must have been created for the same Char (e.g., via fmt::make_printf_args<Char>).
On write failure (std::fwrite writes fewer elements than requested), the function returns -1; callers should check the return value for errors.

functions.name: fmt::fprintf
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
inline auto fmt::fprintf(std::FILE* f, string_view fmt, const T&... args) -> int;
functions.description: Formats according to the printf-style narrow format string fmt and writes the result to the FILE stream f. Returns the number of characters written, or -1 on write failure. Convenience wrapper around fmt::vfprintf that builds the argument pack.
requirements: f must be a valid, non-null pointer to an open FILE suitable for writing.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string recognized by this implementation.
The number and types of args must match the format specifiers in fmt.
Callers should check the return value; -1 indicates a write error.

functions.name: fmt::printf
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
inline auto fmt::printf(string_view fmt, const T&... args) -> int;
functions.description: Formats according to the printf-style narrow format string fmt and writes the result to stdout. Returns the number of characters written, or -1 on write failure. Convenience wrapper around fmt::vfprintf(stdout, ...).
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string recognized by this implementation.
The number and types of args must match the format specifiers in fmt.
Relies on stdout being a valid writable stream.
Callers should check the return value; -1 indicates a write error.

functions.name: fmt::basic_ostream_formatter::set_debug_format
functions.signature:
template <typename Char>
void fmt::basic_ostream_formatter<Char>::set_debug_format() = delete
functions.description: Deleted member of fmt::basic_ostream_formatter that would otherwise switch the formatter into a debug format. It is intentionally disabled for ostream-based formatting to prevent debug-format usage with this formatter.
requirements: This function is deleted and must not be called.

functions.name: fmt::basic_ostream_formatter::format
functions.signature:
template <typename Char, typename T, typename Context>
auto fmt::basic_ostream_formatter<Char>::format(const T& value, Context& ctx) const -> decltype(ctx.out())
functions.description: Formats value by streaming it into an internal std::basic_ostream<Char> (imbued with the classic locale) using operator<<, then forwards the produced character buffer to the provided formatting context. Use this when T is stream-insertable rather than having a dedicated fmt formatter.
requirements: T must be stream-insertable into std::basic_ostream<Char> (i.e., an appropriate operator<<(std::basic_ostream<Char>&, const T&) must be available).
Context must provide ctx.out() and be compatible with fmt’s formatter protocol.
value must be valid for the duration of the call (it is read-only).
Formatting may set failbit/badbit on the internal stream; if a destination stream later has exceptions enabled, writes can throw std::ios_base::failure.

functions.name: fmt::formatter<fmt::detail::streamed_view<T>, Char>::format
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Char, typename Context>
auto fmt::formatter<fmt::detail::streamed_view<T>, Char>::format(fmt::detail::streamed_view<T> view, Context& ctx) const -> decltype(ctx.out())
functions.description: Formats a streamed_view<T> by streaming the contained value via operator<< into an internal std::basic_ostream<Char>, then writes the produced characters to the provided formatting context. This enables fmt::format/print of values explicitly wrapped with fmt::streamed(...).
requirements: T must be stream-insertable into std::basic_ostream<Char>.
Context must provide ctx.out() and be compatible with fmt’s formatter protocol.
The streamed_view holds a const T&; the referenced object must remain alive for the duration of the formatting call.

functions.name: fmt::streamed
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
constexpr auto fmt::streamed(const T& value) -> fmt::detail::streamed_view<T>
functions.description: Returns a lightweight view that refers to value and requests that it be formatted via ostream operator<<. Useful to force ostream-based formatting when no fmt::formatter<T> is provided.
requirements: The returned view holds a const reference; value must outlive any subsequent formatting/printing that consumes this view.
No streaming occurs at the time of this call; operator<< requirements apply when the view is actually formatted.

functions.name: fmt::vprint
functions.signature: inline void fmt::vprint(std::ostream& os, fmt::string_view fmt, fmt::format_args args)
functions.description: Formats according to fmt and prebuilt args into an internal memory buffer, then writes the buffer to the given std::ostream. On some Windows configurations it may write directly to the console for UTF-8 handling; otherwise it writes via os.write.
requirements: os must be a valid output stream open for writing.
fmt must reference a valid fmt-style format string compatible with args.
args must be a valid fmt::format_args object whose underlying argument storage remains alive for the duration of the call.
If os has exceptions enabled for failbit/badbit, writes may throw std::ios_base::failure.

functions.name: fmt::print
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
void fmt::print(std::ostream& os, fmt::format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args)
functions.description: Formats args according to the compile-time-checked format string fmt and writes the result to os. Uses fmt::vformat_to into a memory buffer and then writes the buffer to the stream. On platforms configured for UTF-8 console optimization, it may delegate to vprint.
requirements: os must be a valid output stream open for writing.
The format string must be compatible with the provided arguments (enforced by fmt::format_string<T...>).
Arguments must be valid and convertible per fmt’s formatting rules; any referenced data must outlive the call.
If the destination stream has exceptions enabled for failbit/badbit, writes may throw std::ios_base::failure.

functions.name: fmt::println
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
void fmt::println(std::ostream& os, fmt::format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args)
functions.description: Formats args according to fmt, appends a newline, and writes the result to os. Implemented by calling fmt::print(os, "{}\n", fmt::format(fmt, args...)).
requirements: os must be a valid output stream open for writing.
The format string must be compatible with the provided arguments (enforced by fmt::format_string<T...>).
Arguments must be valid and convertible per fmt’s formatting rules; any referenced data must outlive the call.
If the destination stream has exceptions enabled for failbit/badbit, writes may throw std::ios_base::failure.

functions.name: fg
functions.signature: FMT_CONSTEXPR inline auto fmt::fg(fmt::detail::color_type foreground) noexcept -> fmt::text_style
functions.description: Creates a text_style that sets the foreground (text) color. Pass a color via fmt::color, fmt::rgb, or fmt::terminal_color (implicitly convertible to detail::color_type) to produce an ANSI color escape when formatting or printing.
requirements: foreground must be a valid fmt::detail::color_type (e.g., constructed from fmt::color, fmt::rgb, or fmt::terminal_color).
The returned style is intended to be used with fmt formatting functions that understand text_style (e.g., fmt::print, fmt::format, fmt::format_to, or fmt::styled).

functions.name: bg
functions.signature: FMT_CONSTEXPR inline auto fmt::bg(fmt::detail::color_type background) noexcept -> fmt::text_style
functions.description: Creates a text_style that sets the background color. Accepts a color via fmt::color, fmt::rgb, or fmt::terminal_color through implicit conversion to detail::color_type.
requirements: background must be a valid fmt::detail::color_type (e.g., constructed from fmt::color, fmt::rgb, or fmt::terminal_color).
The returned style is intended to be used with fmt formatting functions that understand text_style (e.g., fmt::print, fmt::format, fmt::format_to, or fmt::styled).

functions.name: operator|
functions.signature: FMT_CONSTEXPR inline auto fmt::operator|(fmt::emphasis lhs, fmt::emphasis rhs) noexcept -> fmt::text_style
functions.description: Combines two emphasis flags (bold, underline, etc.) into a text_style by OR-ing them. Use to specify multiple emphasis attributes at once.
requirements: lhs and rhs are emphasis bitflags; any combination is allowed.
The returned text_style can be further combined with foreground/background colors via operator| on text_style.

functions.name: detail::make_foreground_color
functions.signature:
template <typename Char>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto fmt::detail::make_foreground_color(color_type foreground) noexcept -> ansi_color_escape<Char>
functions.description: Builds an ANSI escape sequence object for setting the foreground color corresponding to the given color_type. Used internally to emit color codes during formatting.
requirements: foreground must be a valid fmt::detail::color_type.
Char must be a character type compatible with the output buffer/iterator (typically char or wchar_t-like when used accordingly).

functions.name: detail::make_background_color
functions.signature:
template <typename Char>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto fmt::detail::make_background_color(color_type background) noexcept -> ansi_color_escape<Char>
functions.description: Builds an ANSI escape sequence object for setting the background color corresponding to the given color_type. Used internally to emit color codes during formatting.
requirements: background must be a valid fmt::detail::color_type.
Char must be a character type compatible with the output buffer/iterator (typically char or wchar_t-like when used accordingly).

functions.name: detail::make_emphasis
functions.signature:
template <typename Char>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto fmt::detail::make_emphasis(fmt::emphasis em) noexcept -> ansi_color_escape<Char>
functions.description: Builds an ANSI escape sequence object for the given emphasis flags (bold, underline, etc.). Used internally to emit emphasis codes during formatting.
requirements: em is a bitmask of fmt::emphasis values.
Char must be a character type compatible with the output buffer/iterator (typically char or wchar_t-like when used accordingly).

functions.name: detail::reset_color
functions.signature:
template <typename Char>
inline void fmt::detail::reset_color(fmt::detail::buffer<Char>& buffer)
functions.description: Appends the ANSI reset sequence "\x1b[0m" to the provided buffer, clearing all previously applied text attributes in the terminal.
requirements: buffer must be a valid fmt::detail::buffer<Char> capable of append operations.

functions.name: detail::vformat_to
functions.signature:
template <typename Char>
void fmt::detail::vformat_to(fmt::detail::buffer<Char>& buf, fmt::text_style ts, fmt::basic_string_view<Char> fmt, fmt::basic_format_args<fmt::buffered_context<Char>> args)
functions.description: Formats according to fmt and args into buf, applying the given text_style first (emphasis, foreground, background) by emitting corresponding ANSI escape sequences and then appending a reset sequence if a style was applied.
requirements: buf must be a valid buffer to receive formatted output.
fmt must be a valid format string for the supplied args.
args must contain arguments referenced by fmt; mismatches result in formatting errors (per fmt library behavior).

functions.name: vprint
functions.signature: inline void fmt::vprint(FILE* f, fmt::text_style ts, fmt::string_view fmt, fmt::format_args args)
functions.description: Formats into an internal memory buffer using the given text_style and then prints the resulting string to the FILE stream f. Uses ANSI escape sequences to represent style.
requirements: f must be a valid, writable FILE* (e.g., not null and opened for output).
fmt must be a valid format string for args.
May write ANSI escape sequences; the receiving terminal must support them to have visible styling effects.

functions.name: print
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
void fmt::print(FILE* f, fmt::text_style ts, fmt::format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args)
functions.description: Formats the given arguments with the specified text_style and prints the result to the FILE stream f using ANSI escape sequences for styling. This is the FILE*-targeting overload.
requirements: f must be a valid, writable FILE* (e.g., not null and opened for output).
fmt must match the provided arguments T... according to fmt::format_string<T...>.
Emits ANSI escape sequences; visible styling requires an ANSI-capable output.

functions.name: print
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
void fmt::print(fmt::text_style ts, fmt::format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args)
functions.description: Formats the given arguments with the specified text_style and prints the result to stdout. This overload forwards to the FILE* overload with stdout.
requirements: fmt must match the provided arguments T... according to fmt::format_string<T...>.
Writes to stdout; ensure stdout is available and writable.
Emits ANSI escape sequences; visible styling requires an ANSI-capable output.

functions.name: vformat
functions.signature: inline auto fmt::vformat(fmt::text_style ts, fmt::string_view fmt, fmt::format_args args) -> std::string
functions.description: Formats according to fmt and args into a string, applying the specified text_style using ANSI escape sequences. Returns the resulting string.
requirements: fmt must be a valid format string for args.
Produces ANSI escape sequences if ts specifies any styling.

functions.name: format
functions.signature:
template <typename... T>
inline auto fmt::format(fmt::text_style ts, fmt::format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args) -> std::string
functions.description: Formats arguments into a std::string, applying the given text_style via ANSI escape sequences.
requirements: fmt must match the provided arguments T... according to fmt::format_string<T...>.
Returns a std::string that may contain ANSI escape sequences when styling is applied.

functions.name: vformat_to
functions.signature:
template <typename OutputIt,
          FMT_ENABLE_IF(fmt::detail::is_output_iterator<OutputIt, char>::value)>
auto fmt::vformat_to(OutputIt out, fmt::text_style ts, fmt::string_view fmt, fmt::format_args args) -> OutputIt
functions.description: Formats into an output iterator, applying the given text_style before the formatted content and resetting style afterward. Writes ANSI escape sequences to the output.
requirements: OutputIt must satisfy fmt::detail::is_output_iterator<OutputIt, char>::value and point to a writable output range of char.
fmt must be a valid format string for args.
Returns an iterator past the end of the written range.

functions.name: format_to
functions.signature:
template <typename OutputIt, typename... T,
          FMT_ENABLE_IF(fmt::detail::is_output_iterator<OutputIt, char>::value)>
inline auto fmt::format_to(OutputIt out, fmt::text_style ts, fmt::format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args) -> OutputIt
functions.description: Formats arguments with the given text_style into the provided output iterator and returns the iterator past the end. Styling is emitted as ANSI escape sequences.
requirements: OutputIt must satisfy fmt::detail::is_output_iterator<OutputIt, char>::value and point to a writable output range of char.
fmt must match the provided arguments T... according to fmt::format_string<T...>.

functions.name: styled
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
FMT_CONSTEXPR auto fmt::styled(const T& value, fmt::text_style ts) -> fmt::detail::styled_arg<fmt::remove_cvref_t<T>>
functions.description: Wraps a value with a text_style for use in fmt formatting calls. When formatted, the value will be preceded by ANSI escape sequences for the style and followed by a reset.
requirements: value must be formattable by fmt (there must be a formatter specialization for remove_cvref_t<T>).

ts can include emphasis and/or colors; if ts was built by OR-ing incompatible color types (terminal color with any color), construction of such a style via text_style operator| may report an error before use.
Use the returned object only within fmt formatting APIs that understand styled_arg (e.g., fmt::format, fmt::print, fmt::format_to).

functions.name: fmt::system_category
functions.signature: const std::error_category& fmt::system_category() noexcept
functions.description: Returns the platform-specific system error_category. On Windows this is a custom category provided by the library; on non-Windows it returns std::system_category(). Use it to construct or interpret std::error_code values produced by OS APIs.
requirements: Callable on any thread; function is noexcept.
Availability is platform-dependent: on non-Windows it forwards to std::system_category(); on Windows it is provided by the library.

functions.name: fmt::vwindows_error
functions.signature: std::system_error fmt::vwindows_error(int error_code, fmt::string_view fmt, fmt::format_args args)
functions.description: Creates and returns a std::system_error whose message is "<formatted message>: <Windows system-message>", using a Windows error code and a pre-built argument list. Intended to be used by wrappers that already have fmt::format_args.
requirements: Windows-only; error_code must be a Windows GetLastError-style code (may be invalid like -1, which will be reflected in the message).
fmt must be a valid format string for the provided args.
args must match the format string placeholders.
Does not throw until constructing/allocating the std::system_error message; callers should be prepared for exceptions.

functions.name: fmt::windows_error
functions.signature: template <typename... T> std::system_error fmt::windows_error(int error_code, fmt::string_view message, const T&... args)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that formats message with args, then returns a std::system_error combining that message with the Windows system message for error_code. Use when you want to throw or propagate a system_error describing a Windows API failure.
requirements: Windows-only; error_code should be a Windows GetLastError-style code.
message must be a valid format string for the supplied args.
Each arg must be formattable by the fmt library (has a formatter specialization).
May allocate and throw while formatting or constructing std::system_error.

functions.name: fmt::report_windows_error
functions.signature: void fmt::report_windows_error(int error_code, const char* message) noexcept
functions.description: Reports a Windows error without throwing, suitable for use in contexts like destructors. It formats and writes a diagnostic combining message and the Windows system message for error_code.
requirements: Windows-only; error_code is a Windows error code.
message must be a valid null-terminated C string pointer (may be empty but not null if the implementation expects C-string operations).
Function is noexcept; it must not propagate exceptions.

functions.name: fmt::basic_cstring_view<char>::c_str
functions.signature: const char* fmt::basic_cstring_view<char>::c_str() const
functions.description: Returns the underlying pointer to a null-terminated char string held by this view. The pointer typically comes from a C string or std::string::c_str() passed to the constructor.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid only as long as the original character storage remains valid (e.g., the source C string outlives the view; the source std::string is not destroyed or modified).
The referenced string must be null-terminated.

functions.name: fmt::basic_cstring_view<wchar_t>::c_str
functions.signature: const wchar_t* fmt::basic_cstring_view<wchar_t>::c_str() const
functions.description: Returns the underlying pointer to a null-terminated wide-character string held by this view. The pointer typically comes from a wide C string or std::wstring::c_str() passed to the constructor.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid only as long as the original wide-character storage remains valid.
The referenced string must be null-terminated.

functions.name: fmt::buffered_file::get
functions.signature: FILE* fmt::buffered_file::get() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the raw FILE* associated with this buffered_file, or nullptr if it does not represent an open file. Useful for interoperating with C APIs that need a FILE*.
requirements: If the return is non-null, the FILE* refers to the currently managed stream; do not use it after the buffered_file is closed or moved-from.
No ownership is transferred; do not fclose() it directly unless you have detached ownership.

functions.name: fmt::buffered_file::descriptor
functions.signature: int fmt::buffered_file::descriptor() const
functions.description: Returns the OS-level file descriptor associated with this buffered_file.
requirements: The buffered_file must refer to an open file; behavior is unknown if FILE* is null.
May throw on failure according to the library’s error-handling policies.

functions.name: fmt::buffered_file::print
functions.signature: template <typename... T> void fmt::buffered_file::print(fmt::string_view fmt, const T&... args)
functions.description: Formats args according to the given format string and writes the result to the underlying FILE*. Internally selects a buffered or unbuffered printing path based on argument locking traits.
requirements: The buffered_file must be open (get() != nullptr).
fmt must be a valid format string for the supplied args.
Each argument must be formattable by the fmt library.
Not thread-safe unless external synchronization is used; mixing concurrent writes to the same FILE* may race.
May throw on formatting or write errors.

functions.name: fmt::file::descriptor
functions.signature: int fmt::file::descriptor() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the OS file descriptor held by this file object, or -1 if it does not represent an open file.
requirements: No special requirements; return value indicates validity (-1 means closed).
Function is noexcept.

functions.name: fmt::file::size
functions.signature: long long fmt::file::size() const
functions.description: Returns the current size of the file in bytes. The return type is signed for consistency with stat::st_size.
requirements: The file must be open and refer to a regular file for which size can be determined.
May throw fmt::system_error or std::system_error on failure.

functions.name: fmt::file::read
functions.signature: size_t fmt::file::read(void* buffer, size_t count)

requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
On failure, may throw fmt::system_error.
The returned fmt::file owns the duplicated descriptor and should be closed or allowed to destruct to release it.

functions.name: fmt::file::dup2
functions.signature: void fmt::file::dup2(int fd)
functions.description: Makes fd become a duplicate of this file’s descriptor, closing fd first if necessary (like POSIX dup2 on this->descriptor()).
requirements: This file must be open (descriptor() != -1).
fd may refer to an open descriptor; it will be closed first if required by the platform.
On failure, throws fmt::system_error.
If fd equals this->descriptor(), behavior follows dup2 semantics (no-op) per platform.

functions.name: fmt::file::dup2

requirements: This file must be open (descriptor() != -1).
fd may refer to an open descriptor; it may be closed first by the operation.
ec is set to indicate success (cleared) or failure (non-zero); caller must check ec after the call.
Function is noexcept and will not throw.

functions.name: fmt::file::fdopen

May throw fmt::system_error on failure.

functions.name: fmt::getpagesize

functions.signature: void fmt::ostream::close()

functions.name: fmt::dynamic_format_arg_store::push_back
functions.signature:
template <typename Context>
template <typename T>
void fmt::dynamic_format_arg_store<Context>::push_back(const T& arg)
functions.description: Appends an argument to the dynamic_format_arg_store for later use with type-erased formatting functions (e.g., fmt::vformat). requirements: T must be formattable for the given Context (i.e., mappable to fmt’s type system for Context::char_type).

void fmt::dynamic_format_arg_store<Context>::push_back(std::reference_wrapper<T> arg)

    b"{}",
    b"{} {}",
    b"{}:{}:{}",
    b"{0} {1} {2}",
    b"{name}={value}",
    b"{:>5} {:#x}",

    b"%p",

    b"{:>10}",

    b"windows", b"unix", b"path", b"generic", b"locale",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "😀", "π", "ß", "é", "Ж", "中文", "日本語", "한글", "🧪", "🚀",
]


def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:/.,;|%{}#xXob+^<>\n\t").encode()
    return bytes(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _utf8_chunk(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII and some UTF-8 sequences
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, max(1, max_len // 4))):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.6:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, r.randint(1, 8)))
        else:
            s = r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
            parts.append(s.encode("utf-8"))
    b = b"".join(parts)
    return b[:max_len]


def _printf_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Assemble a small printf-style string that matches stub expectations
    opts = [b"%d", b"%lld", b"%u %x %o", b"%s", b"%f %e %g", b"%p"]
    return r.choice(opts)


def _compiled_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    opts = [b"{}:{}", b"{} {}", b"{:>5} {:#x}", b"[{}|{:06}]", b"{}-{}", b"X{}Y{:d}\n"]
    return r.choice(opts)


def _join_separator(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return r.choice(SEPARATORS)


def _pathish(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create something that looks like a filesystem path
    parts = []
    n = r.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(n):
        w = r.choice(WORDS) + _rand_ascii(r, r.randint(0, 3))
        parts.append(w.strip())
    sep = r.choice([b"/", b"\\", b"::"])
    out = sep.join(p for p in parts if p)
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        out += b"/.."
    return out[:128]


def _make_sections(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    sections: List[bytes] = []
    # 1) Some plain text or utf8 chunk
    sections.append(_utf8_chunk(r, r.randint(8, 64)))
    # 2) A compiled fmt-like pattern
    sections.append(_compiled_like(r))
    # 3) A printf-like pattern
    sections.append(_printf_like(r))
    # 4) A separator that will be useful for join()
    sections.append(_join_separator(r))
    # 5) A path-ish string
    sections.append(_pathish(r))
    # 6) Another utf8 chunk
    sections.append(_utf8_chunk(r, r.randint(8, 64)))
    # 7) Some literals from FMT_LITERALS sampled
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        sections.append(r.choice(FMT_LITERALS))
    return sections


def _interleave_nuls(r: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Occasionally insert NULs to test string_view size-respecting behavior
    if not data:
        return data
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return data
    out = bytearray()
    for b in data:
        out.append(b)
        if r.random() < 0.04:
            out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)


def _add_numbers(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Pack some integers and doubles in ASCII that stubs will parse as args
    i = r.randrange(0, 1 << 31)
    u = r.randrange(0, 1 << 32)
    d = r.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)
    parts = [
        f" {i} ".encode(),
        f" {u} ".encode(),
        f" {d:.6f} ".encode(),
    ]
    return b"".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build multiple candidate chunks and shuffle
    sections = _make_sections(r)

    # Add some repeated words for join inputs and FILE names
    words = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 8)):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            words.append(r.choice(WORDS))
        else:
            words.append(_rand_ascii(r, r.randint(3, 10)))
    sep = _join_separator(r)
    join_block = sep.join(words)
    sections.append(join_block)

    # Append numbers as text to satisfy integer/double args across stubs
    sections.append(_add_numbers(r))

    # Occasionally prefix or suffix with newlines or spaces
    prefix = b"\n" * r.randint(0, 2) + (b" " * r.randint(0, 3))
    suffix = (b" " * r.randint(0, 3)) + b"\n" * r.randint(0, 2)

    r.shuffle(sections)
    data = prefix + b" ".join(sections) + suffix

    # Interleave NULs sometimes to test string_view length correctness
    data = _interleave_nuls(r, data)

    # Ensure size constraints
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    # Guarantee non-empty
    if not data:
        data = b"{} 0 0 %d"

    return data

# Target data type: null-terminated C string
# Fuzzer uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() which both expect
# valid byte sequences that can be turned into std::string, and frequently
# passed further as const char* (null-terminated). We will generate a mix of
# interesting, valid UTF-8 and ASCII strings, including typical format strings,
# filenames, and error messages. The buffer returned is a single bytes object;
# the fuzzing harness will split/consume it as needed to seed its internal RNG
# to produce these strings, so we provide a rich seedable corpus element.

# Constraints:
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Provide valid, likely-useful strings (not malformed), including NULs only
#   when appropriate. Since many uses rely on C-string semantics and may stop
#   at first NUL, we mostly avoid embedded NULs except in specific crafted
#   cases to explore edge handling where safe.


def _rand_choice(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_ascii(rng, min_len=0, max_len=64):
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Printable plus a few common punctuation useful in format strings.
    alphabet = (
        "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
        "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
        "0123456789"
        " _-.,:/\\+*=()[]{}<>!?%$#@^&|~"  # contains '%' for printf and '{}' for fmt
    )
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))


def _rand_utf8(rng, min_len=0, max_len=48):
    # Build a UTF-8 string from selected codepoint ranges (valid sequences).
    # Keep it short to stay under the budget.
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    pools = [
        (0x20, 0x7E),      # basic ASCII printable
        (0xA0, 0x17FF),    # Latin-1 supplement to some Indic (avoid surrogates)
        (0x1F300, 0x1F64F) # emojis block
    ]
    s = []
    for _ in range(length):
        lo, hi = _rand_choice(rng, pools)
        cp = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        # Avoid surrogate range
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            cp = 0x20
        s.append(chr(cp))
    return ''.join(s)


def _interesting_format_strings():
    # A suite of valid fmt/printf format strings to exercise paths
    return [
        "%d",
        "%u %x %o",
        "%lld",
        "%p",
        "%f %e %g",
        "{}",
        "{0} {1} {2}",
        "{name}",
        "{:+d}",
        "{:#x}",
        "{:.6f}",
        "{:>10}",
        "{:g}",
        "{:%Y-%m-%d}",  # chrono-like (if routed)
        "optional({})",
        "variant({})",
    ]


def _interesting_messages():
    return [
        "error",
        "permission denied",
        "file not found",
        "invalid argument",
        "division by zero",
        "timeout",
        "network unreachable",
        "path too long",
        "unicode ✓ message",
        "Windows error",
    ]


def _interesting_filenames():
    # Provide cross-platform-friendly names and some edge-ish but valid ones.
    return [
        "out.txt",
        "log.bin",
        "tmp.dat",
        "data_0001.bin",
        "a",
        "NUL_safe.txt",
        "path/with/slash.txt",
        "..hidden",
        "spaced name.log",
        "emoji_📄.txt",
    ]


def _craft_blob(rng):
    parts = []

    # 1) Plain ASCII line
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 4, 32))

    # 2) UTF-8 line
    parts.append(_rand_utf8(rng, 3, 24))

    # 3) One of interesting format strings
    parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, _interesting_format_strings()))

    # 4) One of interesting messages
    parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, _interesting_messages()))

    # 5) One filename from list plus some random suffix/prefix
    base = _rand_choice(rng, _interesting_filenames())
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = f"{_rand_ascii(rng,0,4)}{base}{_rand_ascii(rng,0,3)}"
    parts.append(base)

    # 6) Named argument name (non-empty), useful for fmt::arg
    name = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 12)
    parts.append(name)

    # 7) A printf-style format that matches various paths in stubs
    parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, ["%d", "%lld", "%u %x %o", "%s", "%f %e %g", "%p"]))

    # 8) Another fmt format using named field
    parts.append("{" + name + "}")

    # 9) Short string guaranteed non-empty
    parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8))

    # 10) Potentially longer payload for cstring_view checks (truncate by design)
    long_payload = _rand_ascii(rng, 32, 256)
    parts.append(long_payload)

    # Optionally include a NUL-terminated form of one short string as a separate segment.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        nulseg = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
    else:
        nulseg = None

    # Join with newlines to separate logical strings; add final newline.
    text = "\n".join(parts) + "\n"
    blob = text.encode('utf-8')
    if nulseg:
        blob += nulseg

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _craft_blob(rng)
